endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: If updates are required for the Asthma Exacerbation (AE) risk score model or associated data-processing algorithm, thorough testing and validation are necessary.

endorsements.title: The Elastic Electronic Health Record: A Five-Tiered Framework for Applying Artificial Intelligence to Electronic Health Record Maintenance, Configuration, and Use
endorsements.quote: Only after thorough testing and clinician feedback should changes move to production.

evidence.title: Closed-Loop Quality Assurance for Production Clinical AI Documentation
evidence.outcome: Regressions after verified updates to production documentation agents
evidence.effect: Closed-loop verification resolved physician complaints with zero regressions on 42 tracked cases across 1,089 optimization iterations; unverified prompt optimization of an assembly agent produced 18–28 point regressions.
evidence.quote: A closed-loop quality system deployed across thirteen US hospital sites resolved physician complaints with zero regressions on 42 tracked cases across 1,089 optimization iterations, while a deterministic assembly-agent replacement cut H+P trace latency from 19.6 s to 10.8 s (−8.8 s, 95% CI [−10.5, −7.1] s;  n = 100 pre,  n = 100 post).

evidence.title: GRASP: Gated Regression-Aware Skill Proposer for Self-Improving LLM Agents
evidence.outcome: Agent success when each skill-library update is validated by a gate versus unvalidated skill writing
evidence.effect: On MedAgentBench GRASP lifted gpt-oss-120b from 40.6% to 88.8%. Skill writing without validation was no better than using no skills. Adding the same gate to five baselines lifted each in-domain.
evidence.quote: Ablations attribute the gain to comparative proposal generation, the acceptance gate, and the hard regression budget rather than to skill writing itself, which without validation is no better than using no skills.

evidence.title: A Two-Phase Framework Leveraging User Feedback and Systemic Validation to Improve Post-Live Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: CDS malfunctions during EHR upgrade and implementation periods
evidence.effect: Increase in CDS malfunctions found during EHR upgrade and implementation periods.
evidence.quote: In addition, an increase in CDS malfunctions was found during the electronic health record upgrade and implementation periods.

commentary.bottom_line: Two studies, one a single real deployment of documentation agents and one an automated benchmark, suggest that validating updates before release may prevent regressions that unvalidated changes produce. Neither study tested conventional model, EHR, or data-pipeline updates in clinical care, so the evidence is indirect and thin.

perspectives.view: Both tests favor the practice, but one is a level 3 deployment report with 42 tracked cases and the other is a level 5 benchmark with no patients. Small numbers, lack of randomization, and indirectness to general model and data-processing updates lead to very low certainty despite consistent direction.

A Canadian study of 14 acute care facilities found more CDS malfunctions during EHR upgrade and implementation periods, which shows the hazard exists. In one deployment, closed-loop verification produced zero regressions on 42 cases, while unverified prompt optimization produced 18 to 28 point regressions. Whether gating would have caught the Canadian malfunctions is untested.

The deployment study ran 1,089 optimization iterations with verification, which suggests pre-release checks can be automated inside a frequent update cycle. On MedAgentBench, skill writing without a validation gate performed no better than using no skills, and adding the gate improved five baselines in-domain. Benchmark gains may not carry over to live EHR workflows.

Neither testing study reports staff time, compute cost, or release delays attributable to validation. The deployment study's volume of iterations implies automated rather than manual review, but administrators cannot estimate the resources needed to validate every model, environment, and data-processing change from these reports.

Neither testing study reports patient demographics, payer mix, language, or literacy. The benchmark reports no setting, and the deployment study measured physician complaints rather than patient outcomes, so effects on underserved groups are unknown.

commentary.research_gap: No study has tested whether pre-release validation of predictive models, EHR configuration changes, or data-processing pipelines reduces production errors or patient harm in clinical settings. Comparative studies that measure malfunction rates, patient-level outcomes, subgroup performance after updates, and the staff and time costs of validation would address this gap.
commentary.underserved_note: No testing study reported inclusion of Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Validation protocols may therefore miss update-related regressions that fall disproportionately on these groups, and health systems serving them would need to add subgroup checks to their own testing.
